subject: Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5, released 2026-09-22
central_claim: Claude Opus 5.5 is a publishable AI engineering topic because Anthropic primary sources support a bounded E2/R1 claim: the release changes the practical API contract for long-running coding agents and knowledge-work agents through always-on adaptive thinking, preserved thinking blocks tied to model and conversation state, rejected forced tool use, a required computer-use toolset migration on Claude API and Google Cloud, and revised pricing. Performance superiority remains vendor-authored or benchmark-condition-dependent and is not promoted to an independent ranking conclusion.

selection.reason: Claude Opus 5.5 is a fresh September 22, 2026 frontier model release with multiple official primary documents: launch post, platform release note, model page, what-is-new page, migration guide and system-card listing. The selected angle is the concrete migration and runtime contract for software-engineering agents, not an independent claim that Opus 5.5 is generally superior to competing models. The conclusion is bounded because no API call, benchmark rerun or tenant-level availability test was performed.

claims.claim: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 as a long-running coding-agent and knowledge-work model, and the publishable engineering conclusion is that existing Opus 5 integrations must re-check request shape, thinking block handling, tool-choice behavior, computer-use toolset migration, streaming progress handling and cost controls before treating it as a drop-in replacement.

Opened Anthropic's September 22, 2026 Claude Opus 5.5 launch post. It presents Opus 5.5 as the first Claude 5.5 family model, describes long-running coding and knowledge-work focus, lists performance/cost claims, pricing, safety framing and links to the Opus 5.5 system card.

Opened Claude Platform release notes. The September 22, 2026 entry documents `claude-opus-5-5`, 1M default context, 128K max output, always-on adaptive thinking, $4/$20 pricing, availability surfaces, rejected disabled thinking, rejected forced tool use, computer toolset migration and related beta features. The September 24 entries were also reviewed as fresher but maintenance/compliance oriented signals.

Opened the Claude Opus 5.5 model page. It documents model ID, context, max output, pricing, cache prices, default effort, modalities, availability, release date, minimum retirement date, feature notes, fast mode reference and system card link.

Opened the what-is-new page. It provides the most concrete engineering evidence for the article: always-on adaptive thinking, rejected disabled/manual thinking settings, rejected forced tool use, model/conversation binding for thinking blocks, `computer_20251124` rejection on Claude API and Google Cloud, thinking-block progress updates, feature support, fast mode, pricing and availability.

Opened the migration guide. It gives checklist-style request requirements for Opus 5.5, including model ID, adaptive thinking, effort levels, unsupported sampling changes, prefill rejection, computer use toolset migration, default 1M context, and handling thinking in every response.

Opened Anthropic's model system-card index. It lists Claude Opus 5.5 as a September 2026 system card entry, confirming the official safety/evaluation artifact path. The article uses this as documentation existence and does not elevate performance tables to independent verification.

Reviewed OpenAI's September 22 GPT-6 Sol and Luna launch, API changelog and GPT-6 Astra system-card surface. It is a major same-day model release with strong developer relevance, especially pricing, prompt caching and agent cost claims. It was not selected because the September AI edition already covered GPT-6 Astra as the primary GPT-6 frontier release, while Sol/Luna are positioned by OpenAI as cost-tier extensions of that family. Opus 5.5 offered a sharper non-duplicate migration contract for existing agent integrations.

signals.classification: P1 same-day and recent model/API review
signals.note: Reviewed Gemini API changelog signals. September 22 entries include Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Flash-Lite TTS GA plus Voices endpoint updates; September 17 includes Antigravity Agent 09-2026. These are verifiable official API changes, but the September AI edition already covered Gemini 3.8 Flash as a major model/API topic and the TTS release was narrower than Opus 5.5's general coding-agent migration impact.

Reviewed Qwen official blog search results and Hugging Face registry signals. Recent visible registry items included Qwen Image 2.1 and Qwen 3.8 family artifacts. No same-day non-duplicate model/API/runtime candidate with stronger software-engineering decision value than Opus 5.5 was confirmed in this pass.

Reviewed DeepSeek Hugging Face registry and GitHub organization search signals. Visible recent items included DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and V4-Flash-Vision-Exp updates earlier in September. These were not selected because the pass did not surface a fresher official technical package with a stronger non-duplicate E2 center claim for this publication date.

Reviewed Mistral release notes and changelog surfaces. The latest visible September 22 signal was a Vibe experience merge and enterprise migration schedule. It was verifiable but product-workflow oriented and less suitable for an AI technical article than Opus 5.5's model/API migration surface.

Reviewed vLLM release search results. v0.29.0 was a substantial runtime release signal around September 9, with Model Runner V2 default and CUDA/KV-cache improvements, but it was older than the current frontier-model cluster and did not outrank same-week Opus 5.5 for this AI판 daily slot.
